content:
UK carrier Rebel has partnered with TCL to create the Rebel Phone for Kids, a rebranded TCL K70 5G. But instead of running Android with enabled parental controls, the Rebel Phone for Kids runs RebelOS and specifically restricts installing social media apps and has strict control over internet browsing.
Then, there's the Rebel Parent App, which gives parents control over their child's phone. They can approve apps, set screen time limits, monitor the device's location, and even set geofencing boundaries.
The phone does offer calls, messaging, maps, creative and productivity tools, and access to more than 300 vetted apps.
It's an understandable approach given the ever-evolving and complicated digital world we live in. Many countries (Australia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Turkey, etc.) have bans on social media in effect for children under the age of 16, and many more have approved bans that are coming soon. In the EU, restrictions are proposed to restrict social media for under-13-year-olds.
The reason? Because social media has been linked to several serious issues like mental health and anxiety, cyberbullying, harmful content, online predators, and even affects children's development.
Back to the Rebel Phone for Kids. Underneath it all, it's a TCL K70 5G with a 6.8-inch 120Hz IPS LCD, a Snapdragon 4 Gen 2 chip, and a 5,200mAh battery, wrapped in an IP64 body with some MIL-STD 810H protection.
Rebel is kicking off sales from today, and there's a £20 Black Friday discount (with the code Rebel50) in effect until Cyber Monday on November 30th. It brings the retail price of the phone to £160.
The Rebel Phone for Kids will ship between December 14th and the 23rd, so just in time for Christmas.
